messages:
maria: Heads-up — during the HF->Redwood conversion of zeta-1-spm I’m seeing token id drift after the spm->bpe pass. Chat templates that reference <|system|> end up mapped to a different id and the model emits weird leading punctuation.
kevin: can you paste the conversion command and the small repro?
maria: repro command: `python infra/convert/spm_to_bpe.py --spm models/zeta/spiece.model --out models/zeta/tokenizer.json --preserve-order`
kevin: did you use --preserve-order? that flag should keep id mapping stable.
maria: i did. but dump shows reorder. snippet from dump:
```
# sentencepiece id 0: <unk>
# sentencepiece id 1: _the
# sentencepiece id 2: _a
# ...
# after conversion bpe id 1 -> "_the" but our special token mapping expects <s> at id 1
```
kevin: hmm. any special tokens defined in config.json? sometimes tokenizer_class or add_bos/add_eos mismatch causes offsets.
maria: config.json for zeta: `{"model_type":"gpt","add_bos_token":false,"eos_token":"</s>","bos_token":"<s>","unk_token":"<unk>"}` — looks normal.
kevin: are there multiple special tokens in the spm vocab like <|system|> inserted as plain pieces? spm can store them as normal pieces not reserved tokens.
maria: yes — zeta's spm model has both `<|system|>` and `<|user|>` as literal pieces. The conversion script treats them as regular vocab entries and then we later inject Redwood special tokens, which shifts ids.
nate: if you insert special tokens after conversion it will bump all ids > insert_index. That could explain inconsistent ids between model KV cache and tokenizer. Did quant tests fail?
maria: ran 4-bit quant eval on a small prompt suite — perplexity up slightly, and our chat-eval metric dropped ~1.8% relative to HF baseline. The failure log shows: `InvalidTokenIdError: token id 5021 not in embedding matrix` during warmup for the system prompt.
luis: likely mismatch between tokenizer.json order and model.embed weights. When we save the model we expect tokenizer.vocab indices to align with embedding rows. If conversion reorders, row i != token i.
kevin: quick check: dump first 10 ids from spm and tokenizer.json and compare. Also check if we applied any `reorder_vocab=True` in the conversion script.
maria: confirmed: conversion pipeline had a last-minute step that sorts by token frequency and writes tokenizer.json — so ids changed. That was intended to make BPE merges deterministic but broke alignment.
nate: not surprising. For HF->Redwood we must preserve spm id order unless we also reorder model embeddings accordingly. Two options: 1) preserve original spm id ordering and mark special tokens as reserved with explicit indices, or 2) produce a remap table and permute embedding matrix to match new ordering.
luis: permuting embeddings is doable but risky for prod. I'd prefer preserving order and adding a `special_token_index_map` field in tokenizer.json referencing the original ids.
maria: i can patch the converter to add `--force-preserve-spm-order` and include a remap table as a separate file. Also add a CI check `tokenizer_consistency_test` that runs: `python tests/tokenizer_consistency.py models/zeta/` which asserts tokenizer.ids == embedding.shape[0] and that special tokens are at expected indices.
kevin: also check normalization/normalizer spec in spm model (unicode normalization). Different normalizers can change pieceization which hurts chat templates.
maria: good call — the spm model uses NFKC. HF tokenizer wrapper was initially set to NFC in our earlier conversion; mismatch was present. Fixed that locally.
conversion-bot: deploy pipeline note: conversion job #4721 failed earlier with exit code 0x2 due to `missing remap.json` on staging.
luis: we should also audit build configs that add Redwood-only tokens (e.g., <|assistant_resp|>). If they’re appended instead of mapped, that will break downstream evals.
maria: action items: 1) i’ll open PR to revert the frequency-sort step and add explicit `--preserve-order` enforcement. 2) add remap generation and optional embedding permutation utility. 3) add tokenizer_consistency_test to eval harness. 4) run quant + chat-eval baseline after fix and report delta.
kevin: sgtm. please tag me and nate on the PR. add a short repro note so SRE/ops can rollback if needed.
maria: will do — starting PR now. thanks all :thumbsup:
kevin: cheers.
